title: A signed-in caller lists their sessions, revokes one, and revokes all others in one call
asA: operator signed in through the project's Clerk-hosted sign-in surface on two browsers at once
iWant: the account-settings surface to show me every active session, let me terminate any one of them, and let me terminate every one except the current in one action
soThat: I can end a stolen or forgotten session from wherever I am currently signed in, and I do not have to sign in on every device again to clean the list

acceptanceCriteria.description: A `list()` call from an authenticated caller returns one row per active project session, each row shaped per `TAC-1003-security-auth-clerk-session-verifier.interfaces.sessionInventory` `SessionRow`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller signed in on two browsers, browser A holding the active `__session` cookie for session S1 and browser B for session S2
acceptanceCriteria.when: browser A calls the session verifier's `sessionInventory.list()` interface
acceptanceCriteria.then: the return value is an array of exactly two rows, one with `sessionId=S1` and `currentSession=true`, one with `sessionId=S2` and `currentSession=false`; each row carries a non-empty `deviceLabel` string and a `lastActive` ISO-8601 timestamp not in the future

acceptanceCriteria.description: `revoke(sessionId)` on a non-current session invalidates that session on Clerk's server; a subsequent request from the revoked browser fails verification.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the two-browser setup from AC-9112-1 and the returned `sessionId=S2` row for browser B
acceptanceCriteria.when: browser A calls `sessionInventory.revoke("S2")` and then browser B replays a protected-route request carrying its `__session` cookie
acceptanceCriteria.then: the revoke call returns successfully with no error; browser B's next request is treated as unauthenticated by the middleware within the `revocationCheckIntervalMs` window declared by ADR-1005; the audit sink records one `session_inventory.revoked` event carrying operation, a prefix of the session id, and a wall-clock timestamp, and no field carries the full session id or a cookie value

acceptanceCriteria.description: `revokeAllExceptCurrent()` invalidates every active session for the caller other than the one making the call; the caller's own session survives.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a caller with three active sessions S1 (current), S2, S3
acceptanceCriteria.then: the return value is `2`; a subsequent `list()` from the same browser returns exactly one row for S1 with `currentSession=true`; a replay from S2 or S3 is treated as unauthenticated within the ADR-1005 window

acceptanceCriteria.description: An unauthenticated call to any `sessionInventory` operation refuses with `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNAUTHENTICATED` and no side effect.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a request with no `__session` cookie or a cookie that fails verification
acceptanceCriteria.then: each call throws `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNAUTHENTICATED`; no Clerk-side state changes for any active session; the audit sink records one `session_inventory.unauthenticated` event and no other

acceptanceCriteria.description: `revoke(sessionId)` against a session id the caller does not own, or a session already invalidated, refuses without a side effect.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated caller and a `sessionId` value that either belongs to a different principal or names a session that Clerk already revoked
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call throws `SESSION_INVENTORY_UNKNOWN_SESSION` naming the operation class and a prefix of the session id; no Clerk-side session state changes; the audit sink records one `session_inventory.unknown_session` event carrying operation, session id prefix and wall-clock timestamp

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every `sessionInventory` operation emits exactly one structured audit event that carries no cookie value and no full session id.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an authenticated caller making one call each of `list`, `revoke(sessionId)`, and `revokeAllExceptCurrent`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the three calls run in sequence
acceptanceCriteria.then: the audit sink records exactly three events, one per call, each carrying `{ operation, sessionIdPrefix, at }`; no event's payload contains the `__session` cookie value, a full session id, or a raw Clerk claim; the `sessionIdPrefix` field is a substring of length no greater than eight characters
